blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, Hagar was an Egyptian woman, a woman from Africa, living as a servant in somebody else's house in somebody else's land. She did not choose that house. She did not choose what happened to her in it.

verses.text: And Sarai said unto Abram, Behold now, the LORD hath restrained me from bearing: I pray thee, go in unto my maid; it may be that I may obtain children by her. And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai.

verses.text: And Sarai Abram’s wife took Hagar her maid the Egyptian, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nobody asked Hagar what she wanted. Sarai made the plan, Abram went along with it, and Hagar was handed over. That is how the Bible tells it, plain.

verses.text: And he went in unto Hagar, and she conceived: and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When Hagar was carrying that child, things turned bitter between the two women. Sarai blamed Abram. Abram told Sarai to do whatever she wanted with her maid.

verses.text: But Abram said unto Sarai, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand; do to her as it pleaseth thee. And when Sarai dealt hardly with her, she fled from her face.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Sarai dealt hard with her, and Hagar ran. Pregnant and alone, she ran out into the wilderness, toward the road that led back to Egypt.

verses.text: And the angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Look at that. The angel of the LORD found her. She was not looking for God. God came looking for her. And he called her by her name.

verses.text: And he said, Hagar, Sarai’s maid, whence camest thou? and whither wilt thou go? And she said, I flee from the face of my mistress Sarai.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nobody in that house ever called her anything but the maid. Out in the wilderness, God asked her where she had come from and where she was going. He wanted to hear it from her.

verses.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.

segments.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That was a hard word, and the Bible does not make it soft. Her road back would not be easy. But she would not go back the same, because God did not send her back empty-handed.

verses.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto her, I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Ishmael means God hears. Every time she called that boy's name, she would remember that God heard her trouble.

verses.text: And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Thou God seest me. Hagar gave God a name. A runaway servant woman from Africa, sitting by a spring in the desert, and she named him the God who sees.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Years later, after her son was grown into a boy, Abraham sent the two of them away for good.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The well was there the whole time. God opened her eyes to see it. Church, there are women tonight who have been used, sent away, and left in a dry place with a child to raise. Hagar's God is still the God who sees. He knows your name. And he still knows where the water is.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Gen 16:1-13 and 21:14-19 (16:12 left out); tagged sexual implied (16:4 in the verse, not dwelt on); 16:9's hard word kept and named as hard, never used to bless servitude; the angel's words read by the narrator.

cultural.note: Hagar honoured as an African woman God called by name, with agency and grief; no servant-only framing; 'he sees me' tied to 16:13; the close speaks to used and sent-away women without pity.
